briefs.headline: Reds split a doubleheader with St. Louis
briefs.summary: The Cardinals took the makeup game 2-1 behind Luis Gastelum, and Cincinnati answered 6-5 in 10 innings. Emilio Pagan won it at 5-1; Justin Bruihl took the loss.

briefs.headline: Detroit beat the Pirates 8-5 to open the series
briefs.summary: Framber Valdez went to 8-8 and Kenley Jansen closed it for his 16th save. Carmen Mlodzinski fell to 6-6. Pittsburgh have lost two of three.

briefs.headline: Thunderstorms postpone Marshall's match with Ohio
briefs.summary: Sunday's meeting of the Thundering Herd and the Ohio Bobcats at Hoops Family Field was called off for weather. Marshall next play Thursday at High Point.

sections.label: On the Water

waters.read: 1270 cfs - blown out. Stay on the bank.
waters.working: Down from Monday's crest but still four times a normal August flow and rising again on the overnight rain. Nothing here is wadeable. Watch for the number to fall back under about 300 cfs; the seams along the undercut banks clear first, and a heavy stonefly nymph or a sculpin pattern goes in there before anything else.

waters.near: 14 miles above R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 30.8 ft and rising - up and pushing. Expect colour and current; fish the slack behind anything solid.
waters.working: Up more than five feet in a day and carrying colour, so the fish are off the main channel entirely. Shad are the forage: a white swimbait worked through the slack behind the wing dams and in the barge cuts is the first look.

waters.near: below R.C. Byrd Locks and Dam
waters.read: 35.0 ft and rising - high water. Banks are going under and the river is carrying debris.
waters.working: Up nearly eight feet in a day, which is the biggest move either gauge has made this month. The banks are the hazard rather than the fishing; when it steadies, the lock wall and the riprap hold fish and a crawfish-coloured crankbait tight to the rock is the second look after the swimbait.

waters.reading: Sound highs 12:57 AM and 1:33 PM at Hampstead; lows 7:15 AM and 7:59 PM.
waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 12:57 AM and 1:33 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Tide before lure: the 1:33 p.m. high is the only daylight window, and the push into it and the fall behind it are the hours that matter. Mud minnows, shrimp and finger mullet are the forage, so the grass edges and the oyster bars are where a soft plastic or a live bait goes while the water is moving.
waters.note: Hampstead is the sound station and is the read that matters; the oceanfront station at Ocean City Beach pier runs over an hour ahead and is quoted only for a surf read. No water temperature runs today - the Wrightsville Beach gauge returned none.

sections.note: USGS does not gauge the Ohio at R.C. Byrd, and the Corps tailwater data is not reachable from this pipeline. The two gauges above are the ones that bracket the dam, and neither is the tailwater.

kicker: The Ohio is up nearly eight feet at Huntington in a day, and the Williams is still unfishable.
